title: Invisible Languages of the LLM Universe
benchmark_measurement: The analysis measured the digital presence ('digitality') of languages versus their real-world speaker base ('vitality'). In relation to religion, it identified a category of languages called 'Digital Echoes' which includes languages with 'liturgical or ritual functions' that have a disproportionately high digital presence compared to their declining number of active speakers, often due to content produced by specialized groups like clergy.
findings: The paper finds that languages associated with 'historical prestige, liturgical or ritual functions' can persist digitally even as their everyday communicative use declines. These languages, termed 'Digital Echoes', demonstrate that digital presence is not solely tied to the number of active speakers, as specialized groups (such as clergy or heritage enthusiasts) can generate substantial digital output, creating a digital footprint that exceeds the language's real-world vitality.
